topics.name: SQL Queries
scenarios: A cinema database records films, screenings, ticket purchases, and customers.
A library database tracks books, members, loans, and overdue returns.
tasks: Design a SQL query that joins the relevant entities, applies a meaningful filter, and summarizes the result.
Explain the assumptions behind a SQL query that produces an operational report for this system.

topics.name: Database Indexing
scenarios: A logistics database has slow queries against a large shipment history.
A ticketing service experiences increased database reads during major events.
tasks: Recommend an indexing strategy and justify its impact on query performance and update cost.
Compare two possible indexing approaches for the workload and explain the trade-offs.

topics.name: Case Study Requirements
scenarios: A municipal council plans a permit approval platform involving applicants, officers, and supervisors.
A veterinary clinic needs an appointment and treatment history system for multiple branches.
tasks: Identify the actors and key functional requirements, then justify the main use cases.
Analyze conflicting stakeholder requirements and recommend a practical resolution.

topics.name: UML and Design Decisions
scenarios: A vehicle rental platform manages reservations, availability, payments, and returns.
A volunteer coordination system assigns people to events based on skills and availability.
tasks: Develop a UML class diagram with associations and explain your modeling decisions.
Design a sequence diagram for a critical workflow, including alternate outcomes.

topics.name: Project Selection
scenarios: A university must select between three campus technology projects under a limited budget.
A software company is prioritizing customer support, analytics, and billing modernization projects.
tasks: Construct a weighted scoring model with justified criteria and recommend the strongest project.
Explain how changing stakeholder priorities could alter the project selection decision.

topics.name: Project Risk and Control
scenarios: A cloud migration project loses two experienced developers shortly before integration testing.
A public sector application faces repeated requirement changes and supplier delays.
tasks: Create a risk response plan with priorities, owners, and monitoring actions.
Analyze the schedule and scope consequences and recommend corrective actions.

topics.name: User Research and Design Thinking
scenarios: A public transport app is difficult for older adults and first-time smartphone users.
An online learning portal receives accessibility complaints from students using assistive technology.
tasks: Propose a user research approach and explain how findings would inform design decisions.
Apply design thinking stages to identify and validate an improved user experience.

topics.name: Hierarchical Task Analysis
scenarios: A patient needs to book, reschedule, or cancel a medical appointment online.
A commuter must purchase and validate a digital train ticket.
tasks: Construct a hierarchical task analysis for the primary user goal and explain the plan.
Identify potential task breakdowns and recommend interaction improvements.

topics.name: REST API and Middleware
scenarios: A meal ordering platform exposes endpoints for menus, orders, and delivery updates.
A student attendance application provides authenticated APIs for lecturers and students.
tasks: Design REST endpoints with appropriate HTTP methods, status codes, and validation.
Explain how middleware should handle authentication, errors, and request logging.

topics.name: Framework Debugging
scenarios: A Node.js service sometimes sends duplicate responses after validation failures.
A web application exposes administrative endpoints without sufficient authorization checks.
tasks: Describe a plausible implementation defect and propose a corrected Express request-handling flow.
Identify security and error-handling risks and explain suitable framework-level controls.

topics.name: Distributed Communication
scenarios: A remote irrigation controller sends sensor alerts only when moisture reaches a critical threshold.
A warehouse monitoring service polls distributed devices for temperature readings.
tasks: Select an appropriate communication approach and justify the choice using system requirements.
Compare synchronous requests, polling, and asynchronous callbacks for this application.

topics.name: Dependability and Fault Tolerance
scenarios: A distributed payment gateway must maintain service despite occasional node failures.
A hospital alert platform uses redundant servers to reduce service interruptions.
tasks: Given MTBF and MTTR values, calculate availability and interpret the result.
Recommend redundancy and recovery mechanisms and explain their dependability benefits.

topics.name: Architectural Styles and Trade-offs
scenarios: A regional emergency response platform must integrate legacy dispatch systems and mobile clients.
A growing marketplace must evolve from a single deployable application to support independent teams.
tasks: Compare suitable architectural styles against quality attributes and justify a recommendation.
Analyze scalability, maintainability, and deployment trade-offs for two architectural alternatives.

topics.name: Architecture Modeling
scenarios: A digital insurance service integrates claims, policy management, and third-party identity verification.
A national library network needs interoperable catalog and borrowing services.
tasks: Produce a high-level component diagram showing responsibilities and communication paths.
Explain how the proposed architecture supports future evolution and operational quality.

topics.name: Specification-Based Testing
scenarios: A parking fee calculator applies different tariffs by duration and vehicle category.
A scholarship portal determines eligibility using grades, income bands, and enrollment status.
tasks: Apply equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis to derive test cases.
Create a decision table that covers valid and invalid combinations of business rules.

topics.name: Code-Based Testing
scenarios: A delivery fee calculation program contains nested conditional branches.
An account access program uses several validation and exception-handling paths.
tasks: Describe the control-flow graph and determine suitable path coverage requirements.
Explain how branch coverage and cyclomatic complexity guide test design.
